Definition: from G575 and G5563; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate:--depart (asunder).
BiblicalUsage: Once, and it splits a friendship in two. The contention between Paul and Barnabas over John Mark was so sharp that they departed asunder one from the other, Barnabas taking Mark to Cyprus — the word is a tearing apart, a rending.
TheologicalSignificance: A single sharp verse, and it refuses to take sides: two faithful men parted, and the gospel went two ways at once.
